slots.title: Bessent–He Lifeng meet before Trump–Xi summit
slots.body:

slots.title: U.S. session recap — Sept. 20, 2026
slots.body:
The S&P 500 closed up 0.2% at 7,650.50, adding 12.74 points on the session after trading between 7,610.52 and 7,657.17.

The Nasdaq Composite led the major U.S. benchmarks, up 0.4% at 26,522.54, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed down 0.2% at 51,682.64.

The Russell 2000 finished down 0.5% at 2,860.40, lagging the large-cap indexes in the injected close data.

The CBOE Volatility Index fell 4.1% to 14.81, down 0.63 point from the prior close of 15.44, with an intraday low of 14.80.

Among megacaps, $META closed down 2.4% at 665.75 and $ORCL down 2.0% at 147.60, while $AVGO rose 3.0% to 357.61 and $ASML rose 3.1% to 1,679.92.

$NVDA, among the most active symbols in the feed, finished up 1.3% at 222.27; $AAPL was down 0.3% at 336.13 and $GOOGL up 0.6% at 349.54.

$PEP closed down 2.9% at 129.75, with a session low of 129.55 matching its 52-week low field in the data; $PG and $HD were down 0.8% at 146.34 and 299.98 respectively.

$BABA’s U.S. ADR rose 4.3% to 113.26, on a day when coverage highlighted U.S.–China meetings ahead of a planned Trump–Xi summit.

Treasury snapshot dated 2026-09-18 in the feed showed the 10-year yield at 5.0% and the 2s10s spread at 0.25 percentage point.

Gold futures were down 0.6% at 4,399.00; Brent crude was down 2.1% at 101.64, and the United States Oil Fund ($USO) was down 1.0% at 153.82.

The Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund ($UUP) was flat at 28.39 (0.0%), and Bitcoin USD was up 0.2% at 81,362.79 in the cross-asset block.

Overseas indexes in the package included the Nikkei 225 up 1.4% at 65,018.95, the FTSE 100 down 0.3% at 10,659.13, and the iShares MSCI Germany ETF ($EWG) down 1.3% at 42.15.
